title: Derived global sections via comparison pushforward
statement:
For a scheme $T$ and a finite ring $\Lambda$, let $\nu_T:T_{\Proet}\to T_{\Et}$ be the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. For every bounded-below complex $J$ of $\Lambda$-module sheaves on $T_{\Proet}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], the canonical comparison induced by evaluation on the final object is a natural isomorphism
$$R\Gamma(T_{\Et},R\nu_{T,*}J)\cong R\Gamma(T_{\Proet},J),$$
where $R\Gamma(T_{\Et},-)$ and $R\Gamma(T_{\Proet},-)$ are the ordinary right-derived functors of sections at the terminal objects (the etale construction is [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]).

proof.text: Work with the small skeletons and coefficient ring sheaves specified in the pro-etale-modules node, and with the fixed-ring module adjunction of the comparison-morphism node. The ring-sheaves theorem makes both module-sheaf categories Grothendieck abelian, including for a noncommutative finite ring. It also applies to the one-object site with trivial topology and ring Lambda, whose module-sheaf category is the category of left Lambda-modules. The Grothendieck enough-injectives theorem therefore applies to all three categories. For the given bounded-below complex J, the bounded-below resolution-existence lemma supplies a quasi-isomorphism J -> I with I bounded below and termwise injective. The bounded-below-injectives lemma makes I K-injective.

The finite-level comparison proposition gives exactness of nu_T^* on the same fixed-Lambda module sheaves. The comparison-morphism statement supplies nu_T^* left adjoint to nu_{T,*}. Apply the exact-left-adjoint lemma: each nu_{T,*}I^r is injective on the etale site. Since an additive functor takes zero to zero, nu_{T,*}I is still bounded below. It is consequently K-injective by the bounded-below-injectives lemma. Here it is I, not nu_T^* of an etale injective, that is being pushed forward; no acyclicity assertion about comparison pullback is needed.

The direct image is the sectionwise restriction in the comparison-morphism statement, hence is additive and preserves kernels. Sections at the terminal object are also additive and preserve kernels: a section belongs to the kernel precisely when its image is zero. Thus these functors are left exact additive. By the K-injective definition of the right-derived construction, Rnu_{T,*}J is represented by nu_{T,*}I. Since this representative is itself bounded below and K-injective by step 2, one may use its identity as its K-injective resolution in computing the subsequent derived sections. The two sides of the desired comparison are therefore represented respectively by Gamma(T_Et,nu_{T,*}I) and Gamma(T_Proet,I). The K-injective-computes lemma justifies these computations independently of the choices, for the Grothendieck categories established in step 1.

The inclusion u_T sends the terminal object T/T to the same scheme T/T. Its direct-image formula gives (nu_{T,*}I^r)(T)=I^r(u_T(T))=I^r(T) for every integer r. On these groups the comparison is the identity, and is Lambda-linear since both module structures are the fixed scalar action in the comparison adjunction. The differentials are the same maps d_I^r(T), so these degreewise identities form an isomorphism of complexes Gamma(T_Et,nu_{T,*}I) -> Gamma(T_Proet,I). This is exactly evaluation at the final object, the comparison specified in the statement.

proof.text: For a morphism between two bounded-below derived objects, choose K-injective representatives I and I-prime as in step 1. The K-injective comparison principle represents the morphism by a chain map I -> I-prime, uniquely up to homotopy: a roof is replaced by a chain map using its bijection for the quasi-isomorphism in that roof. Evaluation of that chain map commutes degreewise with the identities of step 4. Additive functors carry a chain homotopy h to the homotopy obtained by applying the functor to each h^r, since the equation f-g=dh+hd is preserved. The same comparison principle applied to resolutions of one object shows they are homotopy equivalent under that object; the K-injective-computes lemma makes these the canonical changes of resolution. Consequently the commuting squares descend independently of representative and resolution to the derived categories. The complex isomorphism in step 4 therefore yields the claimed canonical natural isomorphism.

lean.note: The prerequisite had no Lean record. The published side-framework declaration is the canonical Leray isomorphism, obtained by deriving the terminal-object sections identification and using that the exact comparison inverse image has a K-injective-preserving right adjoint. Specialize its Grothendieck abelian coefficient category A to ModuleCat.{u+1} Lambda and restrict its source to bounded-below objects. It requires only Ring Lambda, not CommRing Lambda; it covers exactly the node, with the same ordinary derived sections and specified canonical comparison. No duplicate construction or new module is needed.
